card.title: Ticket contents never reach the model — ticket.md is missing (card handoff) or metadata-only (legacy dispatch)
card.scope:
# Summary

When a SpecKit Pilot card is handed off, the agent running the `specify` phase can't see the ticket's contents, so it stops and asks the user which source to use (e.g. "Linear [TAV-11](https://linear.app/andrew-tavares/issue/TAV-11/speckit-pilot-should-auto-load-assigned-tickets-on-open-import-becomes), suggestions.md, or a ticket.md you'll create"). The `specify` phase prompt tells the agent to write `spec.md` "based on the ticket in `ticket.md`", but that file is either missing from the worktree or contains only metadata — so the actual ticket body/acceptance criteria never make it into the model calls.

# Steps to Reproduce

1. Import a Linear ticket onto the board (e.g. [TAV-11](https://linear.app/andrew-tavares/issue/TAV-11/speckit-pilot-should-auto-load-assigned-tickets-on-open-import-becomes)) — this creates a card with the ticket body stored in the brief.
2. Hand the card off (dispatch it) so the `specify` phase runs.
3. Observe the agent's output during the run.

Expected: The agent reads the ticket's full contents (title, description/scope, acceptance criteria) from `ticket.md` in the worktree and writes `spec.md` from it.
Actual: The agent can't find the ticket contents and asks the user which source to use; the ticket body never reaches the model.

# Context

There are two compounding defects on the two dispatch paths:

* **Defect A (board handoff path):** The normal import→handoff flow (`handoffCard` → `createWorktree`) sets up the worktree but never writes or copies a `ticket.md`. The `specify` prompt references `ticket.md`, which doesn't exist in the worktree, so the agent has nothing to read.
* **Defect B (legacy dispatch path):** The legacy `ticket-dispatch` handler does write `ticket.md`, but only metadata (`key`, `title`, `source`, `URL`) — not the body, description, or acceptance criteria. The real content lives in `card.json` (`brief.scope`, set from `ticket.body` at import) and in `state.ticket`, none of which is written into `ticket.md`.

Net effect: the ticket contents are never materialized into the file the phase prompt points the model at.

# Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Handing off an imported card writes a `ticket.md` into the worktree before the `specify` phase runs
- [ ] `ticket.md` contains the full ticket content: title, description/scope (brief.scope / ticket.body), and acceptance criteria / checklist — not just metadata
- [ ] The legacy `ticket-dispatch` path also writes content-rich `ticket.md` (or is unified with the card path)
- [ ] The `specify` phase agent produces `spec.md` from `ticket.md` without prompting the user for a source
- [ ] Native (non-ticket) cards still work — `ticket.md` reflects the authored brief, or the prompt gracefully handles no ticket
- [ ] Tests cover: ticket.md is written into the worktree on handoff, and includes scope + acceptance criteria (extend `index-ipc.spec.ts`)

# Dev Hints

* `specify` phase prompt: `extensions/speckit-pilot/src/index.ts:34` (`PHASE_PROMPTS.specify` → "…based on the ticket in ticket.md").
* Board handoff (no ticket.md written): `handoffCard` `index.ts:331` → `createWorktree` `index.ts:266`.
* Legacy dispatch (metadata-only ticket.md): `index.ts:1232`–`1236` and worktree copy at `index.ts:1281`–`1284`.
* Content source: card brief via `readCard(featureDir)` (already called in `handoffCard`, `index.ts:339`); `brief.scope` holds `ticket.body` (set in `ImportTicketModal.tsx:29`); acceptance criteria live in the brief checklist and/or `state.ticket`.
* Fix direction: in `handoffCard` (and after `createWorktree` in the queue-advance path), write a content-rich `ticket.md` into `worktreePath` from the brief + ticket ref; refactor the legacy path to reuse the same builder so both produce identical, complete `ticket.md`.
* Related: [TAV-11](https://linear.app/andrew-tavares/issue/TAV-11/speckit-pilot-should-auto-load-assigned-tickets-on-open-import-becomes) (auto-load) and the card model both depend on the brief carrying the full body — ensure the body isn't truncated on import.
